items.title: An exact finite-state representation of viscoelastic memory for accelerated sea-level modeling: SLEvolve v1.0
items.abstract: Glacial Isostatic Adjustment (GIA) models solve the gravitationally self-consistent sea-level equation for the response of the solid Earth and the oceans to changing ice loads. As these models are increasingly embedded in coupled ice-sheet simulations, glacial-cycle calculations, and large ensembles, standard pseudo-spectral 1-D solvers face a steep computational barrier: they evaluate the viscoelastic response by explicitly re-summing every past load increment, scaling quadratically with time steps as $O(N^2)$. Here we show that this computational penalty is an artifact of algorithmic formulation rather than Earth physics. By exploiting the exponential form of the viscoelastic relaxation kernel, we reformulate the viscous response as an exact recursive update of a finite set of modal states, without re-summing the load history. This exact reformulation alone reduces the cost of a run to $O(N)$, yielding a 20.6-fold speed-up relative to a standard full-history 1-D GIA solver for a case study involving a 550-step Antarctic future sea-level projection. Implemented in our open-source solver SLEvolve v1.0, this formulation---combined with fewer, table-free and multithreaded spherical-harmonic transforms, improved file handling, and physics-inspired iteration starts---achieves an end-to-end speed-up of over three orders of magnitude (up to 4,000-fold) against the same 1-D GIA solver, reducing day-long simulations to under thirty seconds on a workstation. Beyond this solid-Earth application, SLEvolve illustrates how human-derived analytical reformulations can be combined with benchmark-harnessed AI-assisted engineering to modernize scientific software. In particular, Numerical regression tests and performance profiling guided the AI agents' implementation choices and helped reject ineffective optimizations.

items.title: Analysis of China's new materials industry landscape and corporate strategic planning
items.abstract: The new materials industry is a strategic pillar industry underpinning China's pursuit of technological self-reliance and self-strengthening. It plays a vital role in the development of advanced manufacturing, the achievement of the "dual carbon" goals, and the security of industrial and supply chains. The deep integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) with materials Research and Development (R&D) is continuously reshaping the innovation and production models of the industry. Existing literature has extensively examined new materials technologies and AI-driven innovation, but relatively little research has systematically analyzed the competitive landscape of the industry from the perspective of industrial economics. Clarifying the characteristics of industry competition can provide practical insights for domestic industrial policymaking and overseas industrial deployment under the framework of the Belt and Road Initiative. Using Porter's Five Forces model as the analytical framework, this study examines the competitive characteristics of China's new materials industry by drawing on publicly available industry reports, existing literature, and online interviews with industry practitioners, given the constraints on obtaining first-hand corporate research samples. The findings indicate that the industry as a whole has high entry barriers, while supplier bargaining power varies significantly across different segments. Buyers and substitutes exert moderate competitive pressure, and the intensity of intra-industry competition differs substantially between low-end and high-end segments. Based on these findings, corresponding industrial policy recommendations are proposed, followed by a discussion of the limitations of this study and directions for future research.

items.title: ANCHOR: Audio-Visually Grounded Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Benchmark
items.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) perform well on audio-visual question answering, but correct answers do not necessarily imply that their stated reasoning is grounded in relevant perceptual evidence. Existing benchmarks mainly evaluate final-answer accuracy, offering limited insight into whether model-generated rationales correctly identify visual regions, temporal intervals, and audio events supporting predictions. We introduce ANCHOR, a benchmark and evaluation framework for measuring grounded-rationale alignment in multimodal reasoning, comprising 2,319 videos and 8,272 question-answer pairs with structured reasoning traces, temporal evidence, spatial bounding boxes, and salient audio cues, including a human-refined test set of 224 videos and 975 question-answer pairs. We separately measure answer correctness, hallucination, logical divergence, and conciseness, with direct spatial and temporal grounding measurements on a focused subset. Across the full benchmark, twelve contemporary MLLMs show a substantial alignment gap: models with comparable answer performance can differ markedly in whether their explanations are supported by annotated evidence. On a matched subset of 100 videos and 446 question-answer pairs, rankings remain highly stable across human-refined, Gemini-generated, and GPT-generated references (mean Pearson r=0.99), providing evidence against model-reference circularity within this subset. Grounding-cue ablations of three MLLMs on the full human-refined test set reveal a consistent modality hierarchy: removing video reduces accuracy by 38.4-41.8 points, while removing bounding boxes (3.2-7.7 points) and audio (4.2-5.6 points) causes smaller, complementary, model-dependent drops. These findings show answer-only evaluation obscures important grounding failures and position ANCHOR as a testbed for evaluating accurate and evidence-aligned audio-visual reasoning.

items.title: Annotrace: A Workbench for Step-Level Annotation of Agent Traces
items.abstract: Every study of why LLM agents fail begins by labelling traces by hand, and every such study builds its own throwaway tool. Observability platforms record agent traces but offer no structured labelling; annotation tools label text but have no notion of a step, a delegation or a tool call, leaving it unclear what the smallest unit of execution to label should be. Annotrace reads six trace formats, including OpenTelemetry GenAI, LangSmith and Langfuse, and turns each run into an ordered, nested list of steps. The annotator writes their own labelling codebook; a frontier model proposes a starting set from a sample of their own traces, answers first, and is asked exactly the questions the human is asked, making annotation a joint human-AI process. Annotrace measures agreement between any two annotators, human or AI. On a multi-agent question-answering corpus it reproduces a previous manual effort's 235 annotation units exactly, and two models labelling the same traces agree 91% of the time at $κ= 0.82$.

items.title: Anthropometry-Based Human-Centered Design and Material Engineering of a Walking Aid for Children With Cerebral Palsy
items.abstract: Cerebral palsy (CP) is a neurological disorder characterized by impaired movement, balance difficulties, abnormal muscle tone, and motor dysfunction resulting from brain damage during early developmental stages of birth. These impairments significantly influence a child’s ability to perform daily activities and lead an independent life. Therefore, providing appropriate assistive mobility devices is essential to enhance mobility, safety, and overall quality of life for children with CP. Walking aids are commonly used rehabilitation devices designed to support movement and promote independence. Many existing walking aids are not designed using anthropometric data representative of the geographical population for which they are intended, which may reduce their ergonomic suitability. This study addresses this limitation by developing a local anthropometric database for Jordanian children with CP aged 1–5 years. Anthropometric measurements were collected and analyzed to support ergonomic design requirements. Based on these measurements, dimensional requirements were established and translated into a conceptual computer-aided design (CAD) of an adjustable walking aid. The proposed conceptual design incorporates appropriate dimensional specifications derived from the collected anthropometric data to ensure comfort, stability, and safety. Jansen mechanism of motion is applied to the new design to promote children mobility. The proposed walking aid is intended to accommodate children with CP within the 1–5-year age group, facilitating improved mobility and supporting their participation in daily activities and rehabilitation programs.

items.title: Anytime Contracts for AI Services
items.abstract: AI services are prone to moral hazard, as model providers can silently route requests to cheaper, lower-quality models, and the inherent stochasticity of model outputs makes this degradation hard to detect. Contract theory addresses moral hazard by designing payment rules that reward high-quality outputs and prevent strategic overcharging. However, existing frameworks assume interactions of fixed duration, whereas AI services are typically consumed through subscriptions and pay-as-you-go APIs that users can terminate at any time based on observed performance. We show that this flexibility can break standard contracts, opening them up to abuse by either the providers or users. To address this, we extend contract theory to account for unknown exit rules. We formalize the problem as a Principal-Agent game, and show that budget-optimal contracts in this setting are proportional to anytime-valid hypothesis tests based on likelihood-ratio e-values. We give an efficient algorithm for computing anytime contracts and show how betting e-processes can be used to approximate them when the models are unknown. Finally, we evaluate our findings on synthetic data and data from deployed LLMs.

items.title: Applications of HFACS in maritime accident research: a systematic review and bibliometric analysis
items.abstract: The Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS) is increasingly used and modified in maritime accident research. This study is a systematic review of the use of HFACS in maritime research. Bibliometric patterns in Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus are investigated. The study used a combination of systematic review, content analysis and bibliometric mapping according to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The final datasets of WoS and Scopus included 60 studies each, of which 55 were common to both databases, resulting in a total of 65 unique eligible studies. The results show a recent growth in maritime HFACS research, mainly concentrated in China and Türkiye. HFACS is still in widespread use, but a number of maritime-specific adaptations have been proposed and HFACS has been combined with probabilistic, system-oriented and data-driven methods. Analyzing the ten most-cited and ten database-specific studies identified causal factors at different HFACS levels and mitigation measures addressing operational and organizational issues. The citation-network structures of WoS and Scopus were different, but the frequently occurring keywords and highly cited publications and authors were similar. In general, the results show that maritime HFACS research has progressed beyond accident classification by the use of adapted frameworks and complementary analytical methods.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Professional Transformation: A Comparative Study of Legal and Accounting Professionals in Mumbai
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming professional services through automation, information processing, analytics and decision support. Legal and accounting professions, which rely on expertise, judgment, confidentiality and compliance, are increasingly exposed to AI technologies, though adoption and perceived impacts may differ between the two fields. This study examines and compares AI adoption and professional transformation among legal and accounting professionals in Mumbai. It focuses on AI awareness, adoption, perceived benefits, professional transformation, ethical concerns, skills, employment implications and future adoption intentions. A quantitative research design using a structured questionnaire will be adopted, with data analysed through descriptive, reliability, correlation and comparative statistical techniques. The study aims to identify similarities, differences and factors influencing AI adoption, providing insights for effective AI training, governance and responsible adoption. items.title: Artificial Intelligence and China’s Cross-Border E-Commerce Development: Threshold Effects and Transmission Mechanisms
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence and search technology is transforming traditional online shopping models, particularly cross-border e-commerce (CBEC), which involves complex customer multi-attribute decision-making with numerous considerations. This study systematically examines the influence of artificial intelligence on the high-quality advancement of CBEC and its underlying mechanisms using panel data from 30 Chinese provinces covering the period 2013–2023. The study found a significant positive correlation between artificial intelligence and cross-border e-commerce. This conclusion remains valid after a series of robustness tests (including removing the interference of pandemic-related data, substituting core explanatory variables, substituting the dependent variable, and lagging explanatory variables by one period). Mechanism analysis indicates that the positive impact of AI on the high-quality development of cross-border e-commerce is realized through improvements in logistics capabilities and the unlocking of consumer potential, with mediation effects accounting for 40.27% and 17.02%, respectively. Threshold model results show that the positive impact of AI on the high-quality development of cross-border e-commerce exhibits a single threshold effect based on the level of human capital; once human capital exceeds the threshold value, the coefficient further increases. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that AI has the most significant empowering effect on the development of cross-border e-commerce in the eastern regions; however, its impact on the central and western regions is relatively minor. It is worth noting that AI exerts its empowering effect more effectively in regions with high e-commerce procurement activity, whereas the relationship is not significant in regions with low activity.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND ITS EFFECTS ON STUDENTS’ READING AND WRITING SKILLS AT THE SECONDARY SCHOOL LEVEL
items.abstract: Although international scholarship on AI in education had expanded rapidly, empirical evidence concerning its relationship with the reading and writing skills of secondary-school students in Pakistan had remained limited. The present study examined the relationship between AI use and the reading and writing performance of male students enrolled in public secondary schools in District Sialkot, Punjab. A quantitative, cross-sectional, correlational research design was adopted. The population comprised male students enrolled in Grades 9 and 10 in government secondary schools, from whom a multistage stratified random sample of 270 students was selected. Data were collected through an AI Use in Learning Questionnaire, a researcher-developed reading comprehension test, and an analytical writing performance test. The study differentiated between productive and substitutive forms of AI use. Productive use involved explanation seeking, guided practice, idea generation, verification, formative feedback, and reflective revision, whereas substitutive use involved outsourcing comprehension and composition, copying AI-generated responses, and accepting machine-generated content without critical evaluation. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, analysis of variance, and hierarchical multiple regression were employed to examine the relationships among the variables. The study provided a contextually grounded framework for understanding AI-supported literacy, assessment integrity, digital inequality, teacher mediation, and responsible technology integration in Pakistani secondary education.

items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence ("AI") is increasingly becoming embedded in activities that were traditionally governed by direct human judgment. Automated systems now assist in recruitment, credit assessment, healthcare, education, content generation, surveillance and public administration. The legal significance of this development lies not merely in the sophistication of the technology but in the possibility that consequential decisions may be produced through systems whose operation is difficult for affected individuals to understand or challenge. This creates questions concerning privacy, equality, discrimination, intellectual property, liability, procedural fairness and the allocation of responsibility among developers, deployers and users. India presently addresses these concerns through a combination of constitutional principles, information-technology legislation, data-protection law, sectoral regulation and policy initiatives rather than through a comprehensive AI statute. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, together with the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, has strengthened India's data-governance architecture, but data protection alone cannot resolve the wider accountability problems created by AI. Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming organizational processes, occupational roles, skill requirements and employee expectations. Although AI has the potential to improve productivity and create new employment opportunities, its increasing use may also generate employee concerns regarding job replacement, skill obsolescence, career continuity and employment security. These concerns are particularly relevant in knowledge-intensive and technology-enabled sectors such as real estate, where artificial intelligence, data analytics, automation, digital platforms and intelligent decision-support systems are increasingly influencing organizational activities. The present study develops and proposes an empirical model examining the relationship between Artificial Intelligence Anxiety (AIA) and Employee Engagement (EE) among employees in the Indian real estate sector. Specifically, the study investigates Perceived Job Insecurity (PJI) as a mediating mechanism and Perceived Organizational Support (POS) as a moderating resource. The theoretical foundation integrates Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) theory, Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and Organizational Support Theory. The proposed model suggests that AI anxiety increases perceived job insecurity, which subsequently reduces employee engagement. Perceived organizational support is expected to weaken the positive relationship between AI anxiety and perceived job insecurity and consequently buffer the negative indirect effect of AI anxiety on employee engagement. Data will be collected using established measurement instruments for AI anxiety, job insecurity, perceived organizational support and employee engagement. Structural Equation Modelling (SEM), preferably using SmartPLS, will be employed to assess the measurement and structural models, including mediation, moderation and moderated mediation. The proposed study contributes to the emerging literature on the human consequences of AI by moving beyond technology adoption and productivity perspectives and examining the psychological pathway through which AI- related concerns influence employee engagement.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications for Early Disease Detection in Healthcare Systems
items.abstract: With delayed access to specialist expertise and subjective interpretation by clinicians and workload limiting the ability to access parts of the pathway, early disease detection is one of the most impactful levers that can be used to improve patient outcomes and reduce the cost of care.Medical image analysis, electronic health records (EHR), genomic data analysis, and analysis of physiological signals are all examples of medical data that can be transformed by artificial intelligence (AI) and especially machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), as there is no way they could be analyzed at the same scale and speed as would be possible by a human being.In this paper we bring together existing evidence of the use of AI in early detection in oncology, cardiology, neurology, dermatology, ophthalmology and critical care.It discusses the mathematical approaches used for their analysis such as the use of convolutional neural networks for image analysis and recurrent networks for time-series analysis of physiological data, and compares their reported diagnostic performance with that of conventional clinical analyses.The paper also examines real-world challenges to adoption, such as standardization of data, algorithmic bias, regulatory approval processes and clinician acceptance, and proposes some solutions.The results suggest that AI systems perform as well as or better than humans in precisely defined detection tasks but will not automatically translate this to better population health outcomes without attention to data quality, the need to integrate AI systems into workflows, and the need to ensure that everyone has access to them.The paper ends with policy, research and system recommendations for maximizing early detection programmatic value while responsibly scaling these initiatives.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Otolaryngology: Current Status and Future Perspectives
items.abstract: Otolaryngology is among the medical specialties most suitable for the application of artificial intelligence (AI), largely due to the wide variety of data generated in daily practice. Otoscopic and endoscopic images, voice recordings, audiological tests, vestibular assessments, computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and digital pathology slides provide rich sources of information that can be analyzed using AI-based methods. As a result, AI has emerged as a valuable tool for tasks such as image classification, segmentation, risk prediction, outcome estimation, and optimization of clinical workflows. Despite growing scientific interest, however, many AI studies in otolaryngology remain at the developmental stage and have not yet undergone sufficient clinical validation for routine use. Currently, the most practical applications of AI involve well-defined and repetitive clinical tasks. These include supporting newborn hearing screening programs, predicting cochlear implant outcomes, interpreting otoscopic and nasal endoscopic images, assisting vestibular assessments, analyzing voice recordings for laryngeal disorders, and improving risk stratification in head and neck oncology. In contrast, complex clinical decisions that require comprehensive patient evaluation continue to depend on physician expertise, with AI functioning primarily as a supportive technology rather than an independent decision-maker. The future role of AI in otolaryngology is therefore not to replace clinicians but to enhance decision-making by improving efficiency, consistency, and data utilization. Successful implementation will require not only high diagnostic accuracy but also careful attention to validation, data quality, patient privacy, regulatory oversight, and clinical accountability. Consequently, the major challenge ahead is not the development of new algorithms, but their safe and responsible integration into clinical practice.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Cell-Based Therapies in Retinal Disease
items.abstract: Retinal degenerative diseases, including age-related macular degeneration (AMD), retinitis pigmentosa (RP), and Stargardt disease, represent leading causes of irreversible vision loss worldwide, collectively affecting hundreds of millions of people. Cell-based therapies, particularly those leveraging induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) transplantation, and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, have emerged as promising treatment modalities that may preserve, replace, or partially restore retinal function. However, these approaches face significant challenges in patient stratification, manufacturing consistency, surgical precision, and long-term outcome monitoring. Artificial intelligence (AI), encompassing machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and computer vision, is increasingly being integrated across the cell therapy pipeline to address these limitations. This review comprehensively explores the role of AI in enhancing cell-based retinal therapies, spanning disease diagnosis and patient selection, stem cell quality control and differentiation optimization, CRISPR off-target detection, retinal organoid characterization, scalable manufacturing, and post-transplantation monitoring through multimodal retinal imaging. Throughout, we distinguish direct retinal cell-therapy evidence from retinal-adjacent, cross-domain, and conceptual evidence. We also propose an AI-powered end-to-end pipeline that connects patient profiling through gene editing, cell production, and transplantation to longitudinal outcomes tracking (a forward-looking framework that needs to be clinically validated in future). While AI offers powerful tools to enhance efficacy, reproducibility, and personalization, it does not replace the clinical and biological foundations of cell therapy. Critical challenges remain, including data scarcity, algorithmic interpretability, regulatory compliance, and clinical validation. This review concludes that the strategic integration of AI has plausible potential to become supportive infrastructure for scalable and reproducible cell-based treatments for retinal diseases, although its necessity has not been demonstrated and prospective clinical validation is still required, and biological insight and rigorous empirical verification remain fundamental.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence as an Organizational Actor: Transforming Power, Authority, and Responsibility
items.abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in organizations is transforming organizational roles, relationships, and balances of power and authority. This chapter examines how AI can be positioned not merely as a traditional technological tool, but as an organizational actor that participates in decision-making, knowledge production, coordination, and action processes. This transformation necessitates the redefinition of employees’ roles and the reconfiguration of collaborative relationships between humans and AI. The chapter first evaluates the opportunities offered by AI to organizations, along with its potential key risks. It then examines the evolving role of AI, from a tool to an assistant and subsequently to a team member/business partner, and discusses the organizational implications of human-AI collaboration. In particular, the increasing integration of AI into organizational processes is examined in terms of power, control, authority, responsibility, and accountability relationships. Finally, employees’ perceptions of AI are addressed, emphasizing the importance of organizational acceptance. In summary, this chapter examines the transformation of AI’s role in organizations and human-AI interaction, with a particular focus on the implications of this transformation for organizational processes, employees, and organizational structures.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Development and Worker Employment Quality: Evidence from China
items.abstract: With the continuous development of new technologies, these new technologies have a profound impact on the labor market. This paper uses micro-individual data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) from 2016 to 2022 and provincial-level macro-data on artificial intelligence (AI), employing a two-way fixed-effects model to systematically examine the actual impact and underlying mechanisms of AI development on the employment quality of workers. The study shows a significant positive correlation between the level of regional artificial intelligence development and the employment quality of local workers. However, this overall effect at the regional level cannot directly prove the individual-level effect of enterprises or employees using artificial intelligence. Mechanism testing further confirms that the effect of the regional AI development on improving the employment quality of workers is mainly achieved through optimizing the industrial structure and promoting the intelligentization of workers’ working mode. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the regional artificial intelligence has a greater positive impact on employment quality for male workers, outside-system workers, and workers in the eastern region. Therefore, to achieve higher-quality employment for workers, it is necessary to promote the deep integration of AI with the real economy, build a multi-party collaborative education mechanism involving government, enterprises, and universities, and implement policies to promote digital inclusion and differentiated support.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Disruption and Structural Enrollment Decline in Economics and Business Higher Education: Longitudinal Evidence from Indonesia
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI), digital transformation, and technology-driven economic systems has fundamentally reshaped global higher education dynamics, particularly within conventional economics and business programs. This study investigates the phenomenon of structural enrollment decline in economics and business higher education during the artificial intelligence era through a longitudinal institutional analysis of the Accounting and Management study programs at STIE Mulia Pratama, Indonesia, over the 1998–2025 period. Employing a quantitative longitudinal approach, the study utilizes institutional enrollment data obtained from the Indonesian Higher Education Database (PDDIKTI). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, trend analysis, linear regression, forecasting analysis, and interpretative analysis to identify long-term enrollment transformation and institutional sustainability challenges. The findings reveal three major enrollment phases consisting of growth, fluctuation, and persistent structural decline. Regression analysis confirms statistically significant negative enrollment trends within both study programs. The Accounting program experienced an average annual decline of 3.356 students, while the Management program demonstrated a stronger annual decline of 5.056 students, indicating higher vulnerability to technological disruption and changing educational preferences. The study further reveals that AI disruption, employability orientation, digital economic transformation, and competency-based educational preferences substantially influence educational decision-making among younger generations. Consequently, conventional economics and business education increasingly faces sustainability challenges associated with declining institutional attractiveness and labor market transformation. This study contributes to the higher education literature by positioning declining enrollment as a manifestation of structural transformation rather than temporary institutional fluctuation. The integration of longitudinal institutional evidence, AI disruption perspectives, and sustainability analysis provides a broader analytical framework for understanding the future challenges of higher education within the digital economy era.

items.title: Artificial intelligence empowering the diagnosis and treatment of rotator cuff tears
items.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being developed for image acquisition, quantitative tissue assessment, diagnosis, and clinical prediction in rotator cuff tears. The breadth of this literature and its methodological limitations have not been integrated across the complete care pathway. Methods: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from inception to July 5, 2026 for English-language original studies applying AI to rotator cuff-related reconstruction, segmentation or quantitative imaging, diagnosis or classification, anatomical measurement, or prognosis. Two reviewers screened reports and extracted study, data, model, validation, reference standard, and performance characteristics. Diagnostic accuracy studies were assessed with QUADAS-2 and prediction-model studies with PROBAST. Because clinical tasks, modalities, models, reference standards, and reported metrics were not sufficiently comparable, evidence was synthesized narratively rather than pooled statistically. Results: Sixty-six reports were included: 35 diagnostic accuracy or classification studies, 20 segmentation or quantitative imaging studies, 9 prognosis or outcome prediction studies, 1 Magnetic Resonance Imaging reconstruction or image-optimization study, and 1 exploratory unsupervised-phenotyping study. Applications spanned Magnetic Resonance Imaging, radiography, ultrasound, computed tomography, clinical or multimodal data, motion video, and emerging sensing data. QUADAS-2 classified overall risk-of-bias as high in 27/36 diagnostic studies, unclear in 6/36, and low in 3/36. PROBAST classified all 8/8 completed prediction-model studies as high risk-of-bias; 1 protocol without model results was not rated. Promising internal performance was recurrent, but selection methods, imperfect or incompletely described reference standards, limited external validation, small or selected datasets, and analysis-stage weaknesses constrained clinical inference. Conclusion: AI has proof-of-concept value across rotator cuff imaging and decision support, but the current evidence does not establish routine clinical readiness or replacement of clinician judgment. Prospective multicenter studies, transparent reference standards, independent external validation, calibration and clinical-utility assessment, and standardized task-specific reporting are required.

items.title: Artificial intelligence for cryptography: a systematic literature review of methods, applications, and challenges
items.abstract: Purpose: to identify, classify, and synthesize the application of artificial intelligence (AI) techniques in cryptography, including AI methods, cryptographic problems and applications, evaluation approaches, challenges, and emerging future research directions. Method: this study employed a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) following the PRISMA framework. Studies were retrieved from Scopus and analyzed through screening, quality assessment, data extraction, and thematic synthesis based on five research questions. Findings: neural networks, deep learning, and machine learning are the dominant AI techniques applied to cryptography, particularly in image encryption, privacy-preserving computation, healthcare, and IoT. Key challenges include computational overhead, methodological heterogeneity, reproducibility, and security validation, while emerging directions emphasize adaptive, privacy-preserving, and intelligent cryptographic systems. Implications: provides an integrated framework for understanding AI applications in cryptography and identifies key methodological patterns, challenges, and research opportunities to guide the development of secure, efficient, and adaptive cryptographic systems. Originality: lies in providing an integrated synthesis that systematically connects AI techniques, cryptographic applications, evaluation approaches, challenges, and emerging research directions within a unified framework.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Smart Grid and Renewable Energy Management: A Review of Techniques, Applications, and Future Directions
items.abstract: Intermittent renewable generation, volatile loads, and concerns over grid stability have become defining features of modern power systems. Addressing these challenges with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) is attracting growing attention, including through better forecasting, automated demand response, optimized energy storage, and smart grid fault detection. This paper highlights the various AI-based techniques developed across the smart grid landscape, ranging from solar and wind forecasting to short-term load forecasting, demand-side management, electricity price forecasting, energy storage and battery management, grid resilience, and digital twins. It offers an overview of recently published work, including the major approaches, namely deep learning (LSTM and Transformer models), explainable AI, multi-agent systems, reinforcement learning, and federated learning, together with their strengths and limitations. The paper also presents a conceptual three-layer framework comprising edge sensing, federated forecasting and control, and explainable operator support at the distribution-utility level; the framework is not validated empirically. Challenges such as data privacy, model interpretability, scalability, and cybersecurity are explored, together with future research directions and the relevance of these technologies to India’s energy transition goals.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Bioengineering: Innovations, Challenges, and Future Directions: A Narrative Review
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming bioengineering, with applications ranging from diagnosis and biomedical imaging to wearable technologies, rehabilitation, biomaterials, biofabrication, and digital twins. This narrative review aims to examine the major innovations, challenges, and future directions of AI-enabled bioengineering, with particular attention to its clinical and translational development. The literature was searched in Scopus and PubMed, with emphasis on systematic reviews and meta-analyses and consideration of other relevant secondary literature across the main bioengineering domains. A total of 57 secondary publications were included in the principal evidence base. The review process was additionally informed by the ANDJ Narrative Review Checklist and an established qualification and scoring methodology applied to the selected secondary literature. The reviewed evidence shows a broad expansion of AI applications and increasing integration of intelligent technologies into bioengineering systems. However, important challenges remain, particularly regarding data quality and representativeness, validation and generalizability, reproducibility, safety, human oversight, ethical responsibility, equity, and regulatory requirements. Future developments are expected to increasingly involve multimodal, adaptive, connected, and human-centered systems integrating AI with sensing technologies, robotics, digital twins, and longitudinal data. Overall, AI-enabled bioengineering is progressing from promising technological applications toward increasingly integrated and translational systems. Its successful evolution will depend on combining technological innovation with robust clinical evidence, responsible development, and appropriate ethical and regulatory frameworks.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in cancer transcriptomics: methods, applications in oncology, and limitations
items.abstract: Background. Transcriptomic data show which genes are active in cells and tissues. Machine-learning and deep-learning methods use these data to classify samples, integrate different datasets, and predict biological properties and treatment response. In oncology, a major challenge is transferring patterns identified in experimental models to tumor samples from patients. Objective. To critically synthesize current artificial-intelligence methods for transcriptomic analysis, with emphasis on oncology applications, transfer of models to patient data, and requirements for clinical validation. Materials and Methods. We performed a critical narrative review of primary studies and methodological papers and additionally described the authors' publication sample for 2021–2026. The literature review was updated through August 13, 2026. Results. The most developed areas include single-cell data analysis, spatially resolved tumor diagnostics, and drug-response prediction. Independent comparative evaluations show that increasing model size and complexity does not guarantee better performance than simpler methods. Clinical translation requires accounting for cellular composition and technical differences between measurement batches, aligning experimental and clinical response measures, preventing information leakage, and performing external validation. Conclusion. Artificial intelligence should be viewed as a data-analysis tool rather than a substitute for experimental or clinical validation. Its value depends on data quality, correct task definition, and the ability to maintain performance in independent cohorts.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Construction Management Enhancing Decision Making A cross a Project Life Cycle: throught A Machine Learning Method
items.abstract: The construction industry, which creates 13% of the world’s GDP, suffers from cost overruns of 28% and delays of over 42%, yet is still undigitized. AI has the promise of transforming management in the areas of cost, time and safety. This research provides a systematic review of AI applications and performs an original machine learning analysis on seven algorithms, i.e., Support Vector Machines, Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors, Random Forest, Stacking Ensemble, Artificial Neural Networks, and XGBoost on 139 Indian road projects with 44 risk factors. XGBoost performed the best with 82.50% accuracy and 84.21% F1-score. The most important concerns were the delay in decision-making (0.152), cash flow problems (0.082) and cost underestimate (0.071). Case studies demonstrate AI’s capabilities: 98.7% accurate cost estimation, 94.36% delay prediction via deep learning, and 97% safety monitoring with computer vision. These findings underscore the importance of ensemble ML in proactive, data-driven risk management, bringing projects into a predictive framework rather than reactive.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery and Development: Current Advances and Future Perspectives
items.abstract: Developing a new medicine takes years of research and requires many decisions along the way. Researchers must identify a promising biological target, find or design a suitable compound, test its safety, and determine whether it benefits patients. Artificial intelligence (AI) is beginning to support each of these steps. Machine-learning systems can analyse large biological and chemical datasets, while newer generative models can suggest molecules for further study. AI can also help predict drug properties, identify possible new uses for existing medicines, and improve aspects of clinical-trial planning. These developments are encouraging, but they need to be viewed realistically. A computer-generated prediction is only a starting point: it must be tested in the laboratory and, ultimately, in people. AI systems can also be affected by incomplete or biased data, may not work well on unfamiliar problems, and can be difficult to interpret. This review discusses how AI is being used across drug discovery and development, what its current strengths and limitations are, and what will be needed for its responsible use. The central message is that AI is most valuable when it works alongside experimental science and clinical expertise—not as a replacement for them.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in E-Commerce: A Theoretical Perspective on Personalization, Privacy, and Trust in the Indian Context
items.abstract: The digital growth and artificial intelligence (AI) in Indian E-commerce, via personalized recommendation systems influenced user experience. The AI boosted customers engagement from marketing point of view also it has increased the conversion rates, customer satisfaction and brand loyalty for E-commerce platforms. But these AI recommendations led to an ethical questions and marketing problems, in places where digital skills, knowledge and access are uneven among the shoppers. For example, when a tier 1 city shopper or consumer is used for tracking data have different outlook compared to consumer in a small town tracked with the same targeted ad feels uncomfortable. Our study was established with the help of marketing theory, consumer behaviour models and AI ethics, synthesizes existing literatures to provide a framework linking to personalization intensity and perceived consumers value, trust and privacy trade offs. It is seen that hyper-personalization of E commerce ads which might enhance participation; might reduce trust when things are not clear. And shoppers have not known as to how data is used. Our analysis with cases data from Indian E-commerce, together with global trends, shows how attitudes differ from urban and non-urban markets, are shaped by socio-cultural conditions and access to technology. Conceptual model used in this research paper, shows different personalization tactics linked with the marketing issues, with trust sitting in the middle of that relationship and data ethics acting as a boundary. To put simply, the model suggests when companies adjust customized offers or messages, this AI and its recommendations shaped results such as loyalty or purchase intent, but only as far as customers feel that they can trust the brand and that basic ethical expectations around data is not being misused. Study emphasizes necessity of transparency, user autonomy, equity in AI-driven personalization and advocates advanced empirical studies to prove the concept across various market segments.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN RECOMBINANT BIOMANUFACTURING: INTEGRATING BIOINFORMATICS AND INDUSTRIAL BIOTECHNOLOGY FOR NEXT-GENERATION THERAPEUTICS
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging in recombinant biomanufacturing, where data-driven approaches are used to optimize complex biological systems. This paper reviews the integration of artificial intelligence, bioinformatics and industrial biotechnology in the recombinant production process from genetic design to large-scale processing. These approaches enhance protein engineering through structure prediction, codon optimization and functional analysis. In upstream processing, machine learning is used to support strain development, media optimization and adaptive control strategies to improve yield and product quality. For downstream operations, efficient purification is achieved through AI-based modelling of chromatographic processes and monitoring critical quality attributes in real time. This is further supported by integration with Quality by Design (QbD), Process Analytical Technology (PAT) and digital twins, enabling continuous manufacturing and real-time release testing (RTRT). Despite these gains, challenges remain, including data limitations, model interpretability, and regulatory constraints. Overall, AI-driven bioprocessing represents a transformative approach with the potential for efficient, scalable and next-generation biopharmaceutical production.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Assessment and Management of Spasticity: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Spasticity is a prevalent and disabling consequence of upper motor neuron disorders, yet its assessment and management remains clinically challenging. Artificial intelligence (AI) may offer opportunities to enhance the objective assessment, prediction, and management of spasticity; however, the current evidence base has not been comprehensively characterised. This review systematically mapped evidence on the application of AI across the continuum of spasticity care and identified key evidence gaps to inform future research. PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, and Web of Science were searched for peer-reviewed English-language studies evaluating AI in adult spasticity. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using NHLBI tools and PROBAST + AI. This scoping review was prospectively registered with the Open Science Framework Registries. The search yielded 1832 records, of which 21 studies were included after screening. One additional study was identified through citation searching, bringing the total to 22 studies involving 1114 participants. Applications spanned four clinical domains: discrimination between spastic and healthy individuals (n = 2), severity assessment (n = 18), risk prediction (n = 1), and treatment response prediction (n = 1). Most studies focused on post-stroke upper limb spasticity. Surface electromyography was the most frequently used input modality, often integrated with kinematic or kinetic sensors. Conventional machine learning predominated, with reported accuracies of 74–96% and the Modified Ashworth Scale as the most common reference standard. All 22 studies were at high overall risk of bias on PROBAST + AI, and none performed external validation, highlighting substantial methodological limitations that constrain clinical translation.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Era of Globalisation: Implications for Students’ Attitudes, Socialization and Career Perspectives in India
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a significant component of the contemporary globalised world, influencing education, communication, employment, and daily social interactions. Its growing presence in higher education is transforming how students gather information, complete academic tasks, communicate with others, and prepare for their careers. This article analyses the impact of AI on students' attitudes, socialisation, and professional perspectives, particularly within the Indian context. The study employs a qualitative methodology based on secondary data, using peer-reviewed research, systematic reviews, government policy documents, and reports from recognised national and international institutions. The analysis shows that while students generally acknowledge AI's educational value, factors such as institutional support, perceived benefits, ethical concerns, and trust in AI-generated information shape their attitudes. Although AI can facilitate learning and collaborative educational activities, overreliance on it—at the expense of human interaction—may raise concerns about social engagement and interpersonal relationships. Regarding employment, AI is simultaneously transforming existing professions, creating new job opportunities, and altering the skill sets expected of graduates. According to the World Economic Forum, the transformation of the labour market by 2030 could lead to the creation of 170 million new jobs and the displacement of 90 million, resulting in a net increase of 78 million jobs. India is addressing these changes through initiatives such as the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, India AI FutureSkills, and NITI Aayog’s roadmap for job creation in the AI economy. The article represents the acceptance of a human-oriented model for mixing AI into Indian higher education—one that coordinates technical expertise with critical thinking, academic honesty, social involvement, employability, and moral accountability.

items.title: Artificial intelligence literacy, artificial intelligence anxiety, and career optimism among university music students: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Objective To examine the levels of artificial intelligence (AI) literacy, AI anxiety, and career optimism among university music students, their associations, and the independent associations of AI literacy and AI anxiety with career optimism after adjustment for relevant background factors. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted from May to July 2026 among students from five undergraduate music institutions in eastern China using convenience sampling. A total of 453 valid questionnaires were included in the analysis. Participants completed the Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale for Chinese College Students (AILS-CCS), the Chinese version of the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale (AIAS), and the Career Optimism Subscale (COS). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t tests , one-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlation analysis, and hierarchical multiple linear regression. Results Mean scores for AI literacy, AI anxiety, and career optimism were 52.97 ± 10.05, 83.85 ± 22.96, and 37.87 ± 8.02, respectively. Students with prior AI training and those reporting more frequent AI use showed higher AI literacy and career optimism and lower AI anxiety. AI literacy was positively associated with career optimism (r = 0.444, p < 0.001), whereas AI anxiety was negatively associated with career optimism (r = −0.461, p < 0.001). After adjustment for gender, year of study, music specialization, prior AI training, and frequency of AI use, AI literacy remained positively associated with career optimism (β = 0.314, p < 0.001), whereas AI anxiety remained negatively associated with career optimism (β = −0.326, p < 0.001). The final model explained 33.0% of the variance in career optimism. Conclusion AI literacy and AI anxiety were independently associated with career optimism among university music students. These findings suggest that students' perceptions of AI-related competence and technological concerns are relevant to their career expectations. Music institutions may consider AI education that combines practical competence with critical understanding of AI's implications for artistic identity, professional value, and future career development. Future longitudinal research is needed to clarify the temporal relationships among AI literacy, AI anxiety, and career optimism.

items.title: Artificial intelligence readiness in fragile states: a systematic review and theory-informed framework for workforce transformation in Somalia
items.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly recognized as a determinant of national productivity and competitiveness, yet the conditions required for its beneficial adoption, infrastructure, institutions, and human capital, remain unevenly distributed across the globe. Somalia, a fragile and conflict-affected state undergoing a prolonged process of institutional reconstruction, exemplifies this unevenness: a young, digitally engaged population and a strikingly dynamic private telecommunications and mobile-money sector coexist with weak public institutions, fragmented higher education, and chronic graduate unemployment. Methods This paper reports a systematic literature review with theory-informed framework development, conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 reporting guideline, that synthesizes peer-reviewed evidence on organizational and national AI readiness, digital-skills development, and workforce productivity, with a specific focus on Somalia and comparable fragile, low-connectivity, Sub-Saharan African contexts. Using the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework and human capital theory as complementary lenses, the review synthesizes findings from 31 sources identified through a structured search and screening process. Results The evidence indicates that Somalia’s AI readiness gap is not primarily a technological deficit but a multidimensional one, spanning fragmented digital infrastructure, weak institutional governance and data ecosystems, a persistent mismatch between higher-education curricula and labour-market needs, and the absence of coordinated national AI or digital-skills policy. Conclusion Building on these findings, the paper proposes a four-pillar conceptual AI readiness framework intended to guide future empirical assessment and policy discussion, encompassing digital infrastructure and access, institutional and governance readiness, human capital and skills development, and labour-market integration, together with a phased implementation roadmap for government, higher-education institutions, the private telecommunications sector, and development partners. The review provides a literature-grounded, context-specific synthesis of AI readiness for a fragile Horn of Africa state and offers a transferable analytical approach for similar settings.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Techniques for Financial Fraud Detection: A Bibliometric Analysis of Scientific Development and Future Directions
items.abstract: This study examines the development and intellectual structure of artificial intelligence (AI)-based financial fraud detection through a bibliometric analysis of 2200 Scopus- and Web of Science-indexed journal articles published between 1992 and 2026. The literature has expanded rapidly, with 89.6% of publications appearing since 2018 and an annual growth rate of 29.4%. Research is concentrated in Computer Science and Engineering, whereas Business and Economics account for 9.2% of classified publications. Credit card and payment fraud constitutes the largest research domain (32.0%), followed by banking, loan, and transaction fraud (14.3%), insurance fraud (12.2%), and accounting and financial statement fraud (9.9%). Neural networks and deep learning, ensemble and boosting methods, and classical supervised classifiers are the dominant methodological families. The field has progressively shifted from traditional data-mining and classical machine-learning approaches toward deep learning, ensemble methods, graph neural networks, and explainable AI. Science mapping shows that the intellectual structure remains strongly centered on payment fraud, while accounting and insurance fraud form more distinct research fronts. Author productivity is highly dispersed, with 88.9% of authors contributing a single publication, while international collaboration varies considerably across leading countries. By integrating performance analysis, science mapping, fraud-domain classification, bibliometric laws, and publication-growth analysis, the study provides a comprehensive assessment of the field’s development, intellectual structure, and emerging research directions.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Predictive Analytics and Simulation Modeling for Environmental and Humanitarian Disaster Mitigation
items.abstract: This chapter is to provide the use of AI and predictive analytics simulations in environmental and humanitarian disasters management. The aim of this chapter is to critically analyze the application of AI in forecasting, planning, response and disaster resilience, and identify problems and future directions. Through a PRISMA protocol-based systematic literature review on Scopus-indexed journals, the chapter discusses the use of machine learning, deep learning, geographic information systems (GIS), remote sensing, and Internet of Things (IoT) in multi-hazards disaster management. A conceptual framework is introduced with multiple layers of data sensing, predictive analytics, simulation optimization, decision-making support, and governance ethics. This research finds that AI can play a critical role in disaster governance through the use of explainable AI, multi-hazards platform, and multidisciplinary collaboration.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-enhanced electrocardiography for predicting mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events: A systematic review and narrative synthesis
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide. While clinical scores provide modest predictive accuracy, the electrocardiogram (ECG) is rarely leveraged for prognosis. Artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning now enable extraction of high-dimensional features from ECG waveforms for predicting cardiovascular outcomes. Our objective was to systematically evaluate the prognostic performance of AI-enabled ECG models for predicting all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). We searched PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar through November 2025 for studies using AI/ML models with 12-lead or single-lead ECGs to predict all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, or MACE in adults (≥18 years old). Eligible studies included adults (≥18 years) using ECG as primary input. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data. Narrative synthesis was conducted due to heterogeneity. Thirteen studies were included (~5.9 million patients). Eleven reported all-cause mortality (8 short-term: 30-day to 1-year), four reported cardiovascular mortality, and eight assessed MACE (4 composite MACE, 4 individual components). Models predominantly used convolutional neural networks [CNNs] on raw ECG waveforms. C-statistics ranged 0.70–0.89 for mortality prediction. Definitions and follow-up durations varied, limiting direct comparison. AI-ECG models demonstrate strong potential for predicting mortality and cardiovascular events with consistent performance and scalability. However, prospective validation and standardization are essential before clinical implementation.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence–Based Gait Analysis in Neurological Rehabilitation: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Background: Gait impairment is a common consequence of neurological disorders, including stroke, Parkinson’s disease, multiple sclerosis, and cerebral palsy. Accurate gait assessment is essential for identifying functional limitations, monitoring recovery, and optimizing rehabilitation interventions. Traditional gait assessment methods may be limited by their dependence on specialized equipment, clinical expertise, and controlled laboratory environments. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision, offers promising opportunities to improve gait analysis through automated movement assessment, pattern recognition, and data-driven clinical decision support. Objective: This systematic review aims to examine the applications of AI-based gait analysis in neurological rehabilitation, focusing on computational approaches, data acquisition technologies, gait assessment outcomes, clinical applications, and challenges affecting clinical implementation. Methods: The review will systematically identify and evaluate relevant studies using predefined eligibility criteria and a reproducible search strategy across appropriate biomedical and engineering databases. Eligible studies will be examined for neurological populations, gait data sources, AI techniques, assessment objectives, validation methods, and reported outcomes. Study selection and reporting will follow the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) guidelines. Risk of bias and methodological quality will be assessed using tools appropriate to the included study designs. Findings will be synthesized narratively, with quantitative synthesis considered when sufficient methodological and clinical comparability exists. Conclusion: AI-based gait analysis has the potential to support more objective, scalable, and personalized approaches to neurological rehabilitation. However, its clinical usefulness depends on reliable measurement, representative datasets, transparent model development, external validation, and demonstrated relevance to patient-centered outcomes. This review will identify current evidence, methodological limitations, and research priorities to guide the responsible integration of AI-based gait assessment into neurological rehabilitation practice.

items.title: Artificial intelligence–enabled nursing surveillance for pediatric cancer immunotherapy: integrating biomarkers, patient-reported outcomes, and long-term toxicity management
items.abstract: Pediatric cancer immunotherapy has expanded from anti-GD2 antibodies and bispecific T-cell engagers to immune checkpoint inhibitors and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy. These treatments can produce rapid, nonlinear, and partially overlapping toxicities, including cytokine release syndrome, immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, infection, prolonged cytopenia, B-cell aplasia, and organ-specific immune-related adverse events. Nurses provide the highest-frequency clinical observations across inpatient, ambulatory, and home settings, yet conventional monitoring often fragments laboratory data, vital signs, neurologic findings, caregiver observations, and patient-reported outcomes. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a means to fuse these longitudinal signals into individualized risk trajectories. The clinically relevant mechanism, however, is not autonomous prediction; it is a nurse-in-the-loop system in which AI improves temporal sensitivity and prioritization, while nurses verify signal quality, interpret age- and development-specific context, reconcile child–caregiver discordance, activate protocol-based escalation, and maintain accountability. This Mini Review examines how biomarkers, continuous physiological monitoring, electronic patient-reported outcomes, and caregiver-reported behavioral changes can support AI-enabled nursing surveillance during acute immunotoxicity and long-term survivorship. We propose a three-layer framework linking immune-toxicity biology, a multimodal digital phenotype, and nursing counter-regulation. We also discuss workflow integration, alert fatigue, model drift, bias, privacy, and the need for prospective pediatric validation. AI should augment not replace specialist pediatric oncology nursing judgment and should be evaluated by whether it improves timely intervention, symptom burden, family experience, and long-term safety.
